subject: Post-demo: StrataScope performance comparison & next lab steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratascope.com>, Tom Baxter <tbaxter@stratascope.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed lab to validate latency/throughput delta

Thanks again for the time today — great questions from the infra team. Quick recap and an actionable plan so we can get apples-to-apples numbers on latency (p95/p99) and tokens/sec.

What we heard
- Primary ask: confirm perceived latency delta vs HyperCloud for request shapes with 128–2048 tokens (user-facing chat flows and multi-turn retrieval).
- Secondary: throughput under sustained concurrency (tokens/sec, p95/p99 under load).
- Constraints: StrataScope needs results with prefix caching enabled and with it off, and with model quantization variants where possible.

Proposed lab (what Redwood will run / coordinate) — goal: reproducible A/B that maps to your production traffic
1) Prompt set: StrataScope sample of 120 prompts (short/medium/long) — you can drop files to the shared Drive link.
2) A/B run: Redwood baseline (r04-gpu-optim) vs HyperCloud public endpoint: 1000 total requests per arm, sustained concurrency 40, target 95th/99th percentiles.
3) Conditions: 2 runs per arm: (a) cold KV cache (no prefix), (b) warmed prefix cache (simulate 5k warm requests).
4) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rates, cost per 1M tokens (estimated), and memory/CPU on the runner.
5) Deliverables: CSV with raw latency buckets, short slide readout, and a mutual action plan for rollout gating.

What we need from you to start
- Confirm acceptance of the prompt set + permission to call your HyperCloud endpoint (or provide a shareable test key) — if you prefer we can supply a client to run the HyperCloud arm inside your account.
- Any rate limits we should respect for the HyperCloud side.

Attachments: stratascope-demo-log-snippet.txt (sample traces we pulled during the call)

Next step: Elena, can you confirm by EOD Friday if we have a test key or if you want Redwood to run both sides inside your sandbox?

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratascope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@stratascope.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed lab to validate latency/throughput delta

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. We discussed with Tom and infra this morning. Quick answers:
- We prefer Redwood run both arms from our sandbox (security teams want the test traffic to originate from inside our VPC).
- We'll provide a short-lived HyperCloud API key and a shell account for Redwood engineers.
- Rate limits: 200 qps sustained, burst 400 qps.

We uploaded a trimmed prompt set to the Drive folder you linked (120 prompts, labeled s/m/l). You should see it under StrataScope/Prompt-sets/2029-04.

Tom and I also asked whether you can include a run with per-request KV cache disabled (true cold start) and a warmed-run where we preload the top 500 prefixes you gave us last week.

Can you also share the exact runner spec you'll use (GPU type, model variant) so we can map to our internal sizing?

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering | StrataScope
elena.ruiz@stratascope.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratascope.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed lab to validate latency/throughput delta

Perfect — appreciate the Drive upload and the test-key route. We'll coordinate infra access via your security contact (cc’ing Sergio to own that flow).

Runner spec (initial proposal)
- Redwood runner: r04-gpu-optim (NVIDIA H100 equivalent, 80GB), 3 concurrent inference workers, optimized kernels, quantized variants will run on an r04q profile.
- We'll include an identical VM spec to run the HyperCloud arm so hardware differences are minimized; we'll note any remaining infra-level differences in the readout.

Plan: Sergio will reach out with an access checklist and an NDA stub for the sandbox. Once we have keys and the shared runner, we aim to start the lab early next week. Estimated time to completion: 48–72 hours of test runs plus analysis.

For transparency attached a quick CSV template we'll use (p95p99-comparison-sheet.csv).

—
Marissa
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratascope.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed lab to validate latency/throughput delta

Couple of technical clarifications from my side before we kick off the runs:
- For p99 measurement stability, we'll run 3 repeats per condition and report median p99 across repeats (this reduces noise).
- We'll capture sequence-length bucketed metrics (0–128, 129–512, 513–2048) and report tokens/sec both aggregate and per-second time series.
- For prefix-cache warmed runs: we recommend a 5k prefix warm window but can change to your 500-prefix list if you think that's more representative.
- Quantization: we'll run int8-ish common QK variants; if StrataScope relies on any proprietary kernels we should know up-front.

If you want, Sergio and I can draft the exact k6/jittered schedule we'll use so the team can preview load shape.

—Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratascope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox access checklist + NDA stub

Elena — forwarding the minimal checklist to provision a runner we can use from inside your VPC:
- Short-lived HyperCloud API key (scoped to test endpoints) or an IAM role we can assume.
- Sandbox VM with outbound access to Redwood test harness (we'll provide SSH key).
- Network rules: allow 10.0.0.0/24 -> Redwood runner IPs for test timeframe.
- Minimum disk: 200GB, memory 256GB, GPU: H100-equivalent.

Attached: mutual-action-plan.docx (MVP timeline, responsibilities)

I'll also share the NDA stub and a signed SOW template if you want that in advance. Once you confirm, we'll schedule the run for Tue lunchtime PDT and send the k6 script.

—Sergio
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratascope.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed lab to validate latency/throughput delta

Thanks all — syncing on the final action items so we have a single source of truth:
- StrataScope: provide sandbox VM + HyperCloud test key, and confirm prefix list to warm (Elena).
- Redwood (Sergio/Jonas): prepare k6 load scripts, runner images, and the p95/p99 CSV template; Sergio will share NDA + SOW.
- Marissa: coordinate readout and schedule a 45-min readout slot next Thu (4/18) to review results and decision criteria.

If that looks right, Elena can you ack and we'll move the kickoff to Tue as Sergio proposed.

Regards,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
